title: multi-sdk: sane credential defaults + lightweight pullstream ergonomics
author: Priya Desai
description: Why: SDK teams have repeatedly landed small opt-ins for auth TTLs, retry jitter, and streaming helpers which left product integrations with slightly different behavior across languages. This causes customer confusion when switching between example snippets and unpredictable token refresh timing in production. Goal: provide a tiny set of sane defaults for credential TTL/refresh, unify an ergonomic pullstream API across Python/TypeScript/Go, and bump SDK versions to publish the coordinated behavior. What I changed: - Introduced `CredentialDefaults` with conservative TTL (9m) and proactive refresh window (15%) used by all SDKs unless explicitly overridden. - Added `pullstream.iter_batches` (TS), `pull_stream.read_batch` (Go), and `async_pull_batches()` helper (Python) as a minimal, common abstraction for consumer-backpressure-friendly batch reads. These helpers intentionally keep the API surface small (one extra helper) to avoid long-lived heavy shims. - Centralized retry presets: `retry.presets.sensible()` exposes a default preset (exp backoff w/ 250ms base, jitter=0.2, max_retries=6) used by outbound auth calls and streaming reconnect paths. - Telemetry: added a small opt-in histogram metric `sdk.cred_refresh_latency_ms` and event `pullstream.batch_size` to make regressions visible in the console; metric emission is guarded behind existing telemetry toggles. - Updated docs and examples for all three SDKs and bumped package versions: python 0.8.7, typescript 2.3.1, go 1.5.0. Backwards compatibility: defaults are non-breaking; all changes are opt-out by explicit configs. Migration: consumers that previously relied on very long TTLs should audit for earlier refreshes; anyone using custom retry stacks can still override presets. Testing: unit tests added for TTL math, streaming backpressure cases, and cross-lang examples. Integration tests run against the mock control plane to verify token refresh under sustained streaming load. CI: initial TypeScript lint failure due to a new helper export; fixed in a follow-up commit in this PR. Rollout: merged to main and will be packaged in the next SDK release pipeline; feature toggles are off by default in Hosted to ensure safe rollout. Related: references ENG-2419 (coordination across SDKs) and ENG-2420 (stream ergonomics).

review_comments: Marcus Liu: Small nit—can we reduce the proactive refresh from 20% to 15%? Customers with short-lived tokens hit refresh storms. Updated to 15% in commit 4.

Elena Garcia: Approve after a test that simulates 200 concurrent streams. The integration run showed one reconnect spike; please add a guard to avoid refresh storms. Added a randomized jitter and reduced max_retries to 6.
Jonah Miller: Verified the TS export fix and example in playground. CI lint addressed. LGTM.

Merged via squash; Commit message: 'multi-sdk: sane credential defaults + lightweight pullstream ergonomics

Coordinated change across Python/TS/Go: credential TTL defaults, pullstream helpers, retry presets, telemetry hooks, and version bumps.'
release_notes: Introduce sane credential defaults (9m TTL, 15% proactive refresh), small ergonomic pullstream helpers across SDKs, default retry preset (250ms base, jitter 0.2, max_retries 6), and telemetry hooks for refresh latency. SDK bumps: python 0.8.7, typescript 2.3.1, go 1.5.0. Non-breaking defaults; opt-out via config.
notes_for_operators: Because credential refresh timing changed, monitor sdk.cred_refresh_latency_ms and pullstream.batch_size for the next 48h after the release. If customers report repeated token rotations, roll the feature back by setting CREDENTIAL_DEFAULTS_ENABLED=false in the private installer config or pin their SDK to previous versions.
